record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.original_question: Let g̃(n) denote the minimum number of products of complete bipartite graphs needed so that every element of E(K_n) × E(K_n) belongs to an odd number of the chosen products. What are the values of g̃(n)?

evidence.quote: Question 13.2. What are the values of g˜(n)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices and let $E(K_n)$ denote its edge set. Consider the set $E(K_n) \times E(K_n)$, regarded as the edge set of the tensor-product-like structure whose elements are ordered pairs of edges of $K_n$. By a "product of complete bipartite graphs" we mean a set of the form $E(K_{A,B}) \times E(K_{C,D})$, where $K_{A,B}$ is a complete bipartite graph with parts $A,B \subseteq V(K_n)$ (with $A \cap B = \emptyset$) and similarly $K_{C,D}$ is a complete bipartite graph on disjoint parts $C,D \subseteq V(K_n)$; such a set is viewed as a subset of $E(K_n) \times E(K_n)$.

Define $\tilde{g}(n)$ to be the minimum number $k$ such that there exist products of complete bipartite graphs $B_1, B_2, \dots, B_k \subseteq E(K_n) \times E(K_n)$ with the property that every element of $E(K_n) \times E(K_n)$ lies in an odd number of the sets $B_1, \dots, B_k$.

Determine the values of $\tilde{g}(n)$ for all $n \geq 1$ (equivalently, find a closed-form expression or sharp asymptotics for $\tilde{g}(n)$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question concerning odd covers of $E(K_n)\times E(K_n)$ by products of bicliques. Related work (Buchanan et al., "Odd Covers of Graphs", 2022/2023, and subsequent improvements by Leader and Tan) addresses the odd cover number of $K_n$ itself, but I found no published determination of $\tilde{g}(n)$ for the product setting. It appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Odd Covers of Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: An odd cover of a graph G is a collection of bicliques such that each edge of G appears in an odd number of them and each non-edge in an even number.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational work on odd covers; the product variant for E(K_n)×E(K_n) is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Odd covers of graphs - Buchanan - Journal of Graph Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on minimum odd biclique covers of graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Published results on odd covers do not provide values of \tilde g(n) for the product setting.
